_about: Authored prose ONLY for the brain map of the endpoint card's panels. Every number on the page is a {token} the generator fills from inventory-endpoint.md · m1-endpoint.json · prisms-endpoint.json; a digit typed in here is a bug. Plain lines follow gabe-lens plain mode. The block names, plain lines and standpoints are NOT repeated here — they live in prisms-endpoint.json and are read from it.

m1Renames._why: M1 was rated on the frozen inventory (m1-round1.inventory.md). The second ruling (D-016, 2026-09-19) DEMOTED and renamed two rows in the living inventory. The join is a rename, never a re-home: the generator refuses to run unless each key is an M1 attribute with no living row of its own and each value is a living row no M1 attribute claims.

m1Dropped._why: Dropped outright by the same ruling. They keep an M1 home that no longer has a row, so the map cannot draw them — stated, never silently discarded.

head.title: A brain map for the endpoint's panels
head.lede: The inventory's {nAttrs} attributes, sorted by M1 into the {nBlocks} blocks you ruled, drawn as a tree you walk. Click a node to open its panel in the tray; click it again to close it. {nSpine} attributes belong to {spineLow} or more blocks at once, so they are drawn as shared and never as one branch's property.
head.keys: In the map: <kbd>Tab</kbd> reaches the tree · <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> move along a level · <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> move between levels · <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> opens and closes a node · <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the last one opened.
head.sketchNote: The sketch you drew has the root at the top right and every edge running down and to the left. Option C keeps it exactly. Option A is the same tree turned {rotDeg}°, which is the turn you asked for: the diagonal becomes one straight axis.

A.name: Upright
A.line1: Your sketch turned {rotDeg}°, so the tree hangs straight down: root at the top, the branches fanning out below it, the tray across the bottom.
A.line2: Depth reads downward and breadth reads across, so a wide level runs off to the side and the pane scrolls sideways.
A.plain: The tree hangs down from the root, and the panels sit under it.

B.name: Sideways
B.line1: The same tree turned the other way, reading left to right: the root on the left, depth growing rightward, the panels in a column on the right.
B.line2: Breadth now runs down the page, which is the direction a long list already reads — the test of whether left-to-right beats top-to-bottom for you.
B.plain: The tree grows to the right, and the panels stand beside it.

C.name: As sketched
C.line1: The diagonal exactly as you drew it: root at the top right, every edge running down and to the left at {rotDeg}°.
C.line2: It is kept honestly so the turn is visible — the same node positions as Upright, rotated, and nothing else changed.
C.plain: The tree runs across the corner of the page, the way you drew it.

D.name: Radial
D.line1: The root in the middle, the branches around it, depth growing outward in rings; the tray sits below the circle.
D.line2: Every branch is the same distance from the root, so none of them looks more important than another — which also means order stops carrying meaning.
D.plain: The root sits in the middle and the branches circle it.

E.name: Indented
E.line1: No drawing at all: a nested list, one line per node, indented by depth.
E.line2: The control that says whether the tree earns its space — if this reads as well, the picture is decoration.
E.plain: A plain indented list, with no picture.

layout.label: Placement
layout.plain: Where the same nodes are put. Nothing else changes.

group.label: Grouping
group.plain: What the first level under the root is.

spine.label: Shared attributes
spine.plain: How an attribute that belongs to several blocks is drawn.

flat.name: Flat
flat.plain: Every block sits directly under the root, with its attributes below it.

standpoint.name: By standpoint
standpoint.plain: The blocks gather under the standpoint each one names, in your words.

section.name: By section
section.plain: The inventory's own seven groups, with each attribute under the one it was written in.

nodes.name: Shared nodes
nodes.note: drawn in every block that needs it
nodes.plain: A shared attribute appears under each block that needs it, marked as shared.

band.name: One band
band.plain: Every shared attribute is lifted out into one band under the root, with a faint wire to each block that needs it.

below.name: Below
below.plain: The panels sit in a tray across the bottom, with the sweep coming down to them.

beside.name: Beside
beside.plain: The panels stand in a column at the right, with the sweep coming across to them.

node.plain: A place in the map. The number beside the name is how many attributes it holds.

shared.plain: An attribute several blocks need, so no single block owns it.

added.plain: A row written into the inventory after M1 was rated, so nothing has placed it in a block yet.

open.plain: An opened node: its panel is in the tray and its branch is lit.

sweep.plain: The line that says which part of the map the panels below belong to.

replay.plain: Runs the opening move again from the start.

more.plain: How the map knows what it draws — kept off the face on purpose.

copy.plain: Your picks as text, placed on the clipboard for pasting into the chat.

reset.plain: A clean slate — every pick and every opened panel is cleared.

pick.plain: The placement you want kept. One only.

map.title: The map
map.n: click a node to open its panel

reads.title: What it draws
reads.n: every count measured from the inventory

strings.rootPlain: Everything one endpoint's card could show, gathered in one place.
strings.addedPlain: Rows written into the inventory after M1 was rated. No block claims them, and nothing here guesses one.
strings.trayEmpty: Nothing is open. Click a node in the map and its panel appears here.
strings.noNeedRated: No question was recorded as needing this one on its own.
strings.noNeedUnrated: M1 never saw this row, so no question is recorded against it yet.
strings.moreShow: Show how the map knows this
strings.moreHide: Hide how the map knows this
strings.deepNote: {n} attributes sit one level below the {nLevels} this map draws. They are not drawn: they open in the block's panel instead.
strings.openWhy: Every place the agent chose something you have not ruled. Named here rather than buried in a commit message.
strings.foot: Inventory {invHash} · M1 cells {cellsHash} · {nAttrs} attributes · {nBlocks} blocks · {nSpine} shared · {nAdded} not placed.

reads.depthRule: The map draws {nLevels} levels and no more, which is your ruling on the command card. A grouping that would put attributes on a fourth level does not draw them: they open in the block's panel instead, and the line under the map says how many are waiting there.
reads.spine: An attribute the map calls shared is needed by {spineLow} or more of the {nBlocks} blocks. {nSpine} attributes qualify; “{topSpine}” is the extreme, needed by {topSpineIn}.
reads.added: {nAdded} of the {nAttrs} rows are claimed by no block: no question in the matrix uses them. They hang off the root in a branch of their own rather than being guessed into one.
reads.addedNone: Every one of the {nAttrs} rows is claimed: {nPlacedOwn} sit in a block of their own and {nSpine} are shared. Nothing hangs loose, so the map draws no branch for the unplaced.
reads.dropped: {nDropped} attributes M1 placed no longer have a row in the inventory, so they are drawn nowhere: {droppedNames}.

map: A branch's number is the attributes it holds, so a fat branch is a panel with a lot in it before you open anything.
The tray keeps what you opened in the order you opened it, so the last thing you looked at is the last panel.
{nSpine} attributes are drawn shared. Under one grouping they sit in several branches at once; under the other they sit once, in a band. Both are the same fact drawn two ways.
options: Each placement draws the same {nNodesFlat} nodes when nothing is open. Only where they sit changes.
The widest placement needs {widest} across; the tallest needs {tallest} down. The pane scrolls rather than shrinking the type below the floor.
Indented is the control. If it answers as fast as the pictures, the pictures are spending space for nothing.

open._why: Every place the agent chose something you have not ruled. Named here rather than buried in a commit message.

items.q: The grouping you asked for was “your six stages”. Nothing in the data maps a block to a stage.
items.did: Built the grouping from the inventory's own {nSections} sections instead, and labelled it that way. A block's section is the one most of its attributes were written in, ties broken by the inventory's order.
items.ask: Either rule a stage for each of the {nBlocks} blocks, or keep the sections.

items.q: You said “the four standpoints the blocks name”. The blocks name {nGroups}.
items.did: Grouped by all {nGroups}, each one read off the block's own standpoint sentence. Two pairs of blocks share a standpoint, and {nUnnamed} blocks say none of your standpoints names them.
items.ask: Tell me which four, or accept {nGroups}.

items.q: Which node the sweep starts from when more than one is open.
items.did: The sweep starts at the node opened last, so it follows where you are rather than where you were.
items.ask: Say if it should stay on the first one instead.

items.did: A panel for the card as a whole: the counts, and the blocks in order of how many attributes they hold.
items.ask: Say if the root should open nothing at all.

items.q: Whether opening a second branch closes the first.
items.did: It does not. The tray grows, and a node closes only when you click it again or press Escape.
items.ask: Say if one open branch at a time reads better.

more._why: D-017: a fact about how the MAP knows something never sits on the face. Everything in this section is that kind of fact.
lines: The blocks are M1's: {nQuestions} questions clustered by which attributes they need, cut at the widest drop in the ladder. The cells are {cellsHash}, the inventory {invHash}.

An attribute's block is the one M1 measured, never one chosen here. {nPlacedOwn} attributes have a block of their own, {nSpine} are shared across {spineLow} or more, and {nAdded} have none because they were written after the rating.
Two attributes are joined to M1 across a rename from the second ruling: {renames}. The generator stops if either side of a rename stops being true.
The standpoint groups are read off each block's own standpoint sentence in prisms-endpoint.json, by phrase, not by a list kept here.
Option C is option A's node positions turned {rotDeg}°, computed, not drawn by hand. Turning C back by {rotDeg}° gives A to the pixel.

pickIntro: Pick the placement you want, set the three switches the way you want them kept, and copy the text.
